judge: Claude Code subagent, Claude Opus 5.5, fresh

items.label: A
items.critique: A single colloquial tic ('mate') repeated without shame, a petty grievance (boots stolen while bathing) and a blunt 'damn fine spell' reward: plain, comic, and exactly Nox's register.

items.label: B
items.critique: Absurd stakes (a pet frog in a burning house) and the one-sided 'What's that you say? Loads and loads of money?' joke are classic Westwood; the journal is short and functional.

items.label: C
items.critique: Reads as a pastiche: the scream opener, then a clause-heavy logistics line ('I can keep the miners out, but you'll have to wade in yourself when you reach the pool down the west tunnel') and a thanks that echoes stock Nox gratitude almost verbatim before a cute closing beat.

items.label: D
items.critique: Opener is a headline-like fragment with a crafted punchline about unwashed shirts and a double-hyphen dash; the thanks swerves to an unexplained warning about a third person, a non sequitur that feels assembled rather than spoken.

items.label: E
items.critique: Polite set-up with precise directions ('which lies in the cellar under the north wing'), a cleverly coded hint (chests that bite) and a double-hyphen aside; the journal spells out the mechanic ('Lure ... out ... and destroy'), more designed than Nox's plain orders.

items.label: F
items.critique: Two voices spliced: an urgent bellows plea plus a shop pointer, then a sly mercenary speech that ignores the urgency; the 'Heh, heh, heh' and 'Ha-HA!' feel borrowed, and the two-sentence journal adds a hint Nox wouldn't.

items.label: G
items.critique: Exclamatory, slightly theatrical mayor ('worse than the pox!'), direct directions ('there, through the double doors'), the reward of a new title and free passage, and a terse journal: authentic campaign text.

items.label: H
items.critique: Lines don't follow each other ('You're not from around here' then trap lore; 'Really gone?' after already paying), the backstory of traps built against thirsty soldiers is invented colour, and the journal carries extra geography.

items.label: I
items.critique: Plain exposition with a cause-and-effect chain (urchin aggravated the bats), an item handed over mid-offer, and the petition as the reward that opens the next area: Nox's quest-gate shape in its plain voice.

items.label: J
items.critique: Conversational opener that continues a prior exchange ('Actually, business has been somewhat slow'), stated sum '100 in gold!', 'young sir' and 'filthy paws': period-plain and slightly stiff in the Westwood way.

tells: New texts pack precise spatial directions and lore into the offer or journal (which wing, which tunnel, what the cellar runs beneath); Westwood's give one plain pointer ('there, through the double doors') and short imperative journals.

New texts splice stock Nox beats (a scream opener, 'How will I ever repay you', a cackle, 'Ha-HA!') onto lines that don't flow from them, so speeches read as assembled rather than spoken by one person in one moment.

New texts tend toward written cleverness (coded hints like chests that bite, punchline asides after a double-hyphen dash) where Westwood's humour is broad and character-driven (a pet frog, 'Loads and loads of money?', boots stolen while bathing).

Westwood's quest givers have one consistent tic or voice per speaker and a reward stated plainly and tied to progress (a spell, a title, a petition, a sum); new texts' thanks drift into non sequiturs or second thoughts after the payment.
New journals sometimes add a second sentence of hints or omit the terminal period inconsistently; Westwood's are one short imperative sentence.
